props.gloss_en: the mishnah: one who says 'we give thanks, we give thanks' -- they silence him
R' Zeira: whoever says 'shema, shema' is like one who says 'modim, modim'
the baraita: one who reads the Shema and doubles it -- this is reprehensible
Abaye: is there familiarity toward Heaven? if he did not direct his mind at first, we strike him with a smith's hammer until he directs his mind

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: הקורא את שמע וכופלה הרי זה מגונה -- מגונה הוא דהוי, שתוקי לא משתקינן ליה: reprehensible it is, but they do not silence him

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דאמר מילתא מילתא ותני לה, והא דאמר פסוקא פסוקא ותני ליה -- the baraita (reprehensible only) is one who says each word and repeats it; R' Zeira (silenced) is one who says each verse and repeats it

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי: ודילמא מעיקרא לא כוון דעתיה, ולבסוף כוון דעתיה -- perhaps at first he did not direct his mind and at the end he did, so why silence him?

answered_by.gloss_en: חברותא כלפי שמיא מי איכא?! -- one may not treat Heaven with such familiarity; if he did not direct his mind at first, we strike him with a smith's hammer until he does (= p_machinan_bemarzafta)
